scene_description: A compact kitchen-like interior with a tiled back wall, a black glass-front appliance beside an electric range, a white open shelf, a doorway and foreground counters. The candidate reproduces the principal arrangement in a simplified, zoomed-out cutaway view.

visible_objects.observations: Both images show a dark appliance to the left of a four-burner range, a white cubby shelf to its right, a framed wall feature above, a right-side doorway and white counter, and a dark foreground counter. The reference additionally shows detailed reflections, appliance hardware and richly textured surfaces that are simplified in the candidate.
visible_objects.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, central back wall and foreground.

spatial_relations_and_orientation.observations: The left-to-right sequence of appliance, range, shelf and doorway is retained. The right white counter projects toward the viewer and the dark counter occupies the foreground in both. In the candidate the scene is framed as an isolated room fragment, making the fixtures appear farther away and their spacing easier to see.

proportions_and_occlusion.observations: The reference appliances fill much of the image height, while the candidate appliances are small within a broad view. The candidate dark foreground island blocks a larger part of the floor and the right counter is more completely visible. The candidate shelf looks narrower and taller relative to the range, with prominent vertical partitions.

materials_and_texture.observations: The reference wall has dark golden-brown, mottled reflective tiles; the candidate has lighter pastel tan tiles with little mottling. The reference floor has pronounced dark wood grain, while the candidate floor is pale and nearly uniform. Reference appliances have reflective dark glass and metallic trim; candidate surfaces are comparatively flat and simplified. The reference right counter has pale marble-like veining, largely absent in the candidate.

visible_geometry.observations: The candidate preserves the basic four circular cooktop elements and oven door but simplifies the reference's sloped control panel, knobs, handle, and reflective glazing. The left appliance has a prominent regular front grid in the candidate rather than the reference's glass front with visible interior racks. The framed wall feature lacks the reference's detailed reflected cabinetry and doorway.

camera_and_composition.observations: The reference is a close, elevated interior perspective with surrounding surfaces reaching the frame edges. The candidate is a substantially wider, more distant elevated view, showing the outer edges of a freestanding wall and floor against a dark background. This is a dominant mismatch in composition.

lighting_and_shadows.observations: The reference has strong warm illumination, specular reflections on the appliances, and a bright doorway and floor strip. The candidate has softer, flatter lighting, a dark gray background, and less pronounced reflective contrast; its doorway is largely brown rather than brightly luminous.

objects_regions.observation: Close enclosed interior in reference versus a distant isolated cutaway with exposed outer boundaries in candidate.
Reference range has four dark burners, two large knobs, metallic control panel and reflective oven; candidate preserves the basic form but renders it smaller and more simply.
Reference has dark glass and internal-looking racks; candidate has a much smaller, visibly gridded front.
Dark mottled golden tiles in reference contrast with the candidate's light pastel, more uniform tiles.
Reference shows a dark frame with a detailed reflection of white cabinets and a door; candidate has a flat gray rectangle with two white patches.
White compartmented shelf occurs to the right of the range in both; candidate partitions and apparent proportions differ.
Reference doorway has a bright opening with a dark lower region and visible brown door; candidate doorway appears mostly brown and is partly covered by a large white overhead block.
Both show a white counter extending forward on the right, but the candidate shows more of its simple untextured rectangular form and lacks obvious veining.
Reference shows a close cropped reflective dark top; candidate shows a larger portion of the top and a substantial light base.
Reference floor is dark brown with visible wood grain, unlike the candidate's pale, relatively smooth floor.

most_important_visible_defects: The zoomed-out cutaway camera and exposed dark background substantially change the reference composition.
The wall and floor are much lighter and lack the reference's dark mottled tile and wood-grain appearance.
Appliance detailing, reflective glass, mirror content and the brightly lit doorway are simplified or visually different.
uncertainty: The left appliance's exact function is not established by the visible front alone.
Hidden surfaces, physical contacts, absolute dimensions and symmetry cannot be reliably determined from these images.
Some apparent size and spacing differences may result from the different camera viewpoints.
limitations: Assessment is based only on the two supplied RGB images; regions are approximate normalized image coordinates. No unseen geometry or ground-truth implementation was examined.
